description: Handwritten teaching collection. Binary relevance labels are declared by the author, not benchmark judgments.

documents.D01: Search engines rank documents for a user query. Ranking helps users find relevant information.
documents.D02: An inverted index maps each term to documents. The index supports fast search over a collection.
documents.D03: A web crawler downloads web pages and follows links. Crawling collects pages for a search engine.
documents.D04: Language models assign probabilities to sequences of words. A unigram model uses individual word counts.
documents.D05: Query likelihood ranks documents using a document language model. It estimates the probability of the query.
documents.D06: Smoothing gives probability to unseen words. Dirichlet smoothing combines document counts with collection probabilities.
documents.D07: A bigram language model predicts a word using the previous word. Bigrams preserve local word order.
documents.D08: TF IDF weights terms using term frequency and inverse document frequency. Cosine similarity compares document and query vectors.
documents.D09: BM25 is a ranking function with term frequency saturation and document length normalization.
documents.D10: Relevance feedback expands a query using relevant documents. Expansion can reduce vocabulary mismatch in search.
documents.D11: Neural embeddings represent semantic meaning. Dense retrieval can match related words with different spellings.
documents.D12: Perplexity evaluates how well a language model predicts held out text. Lower perplexity means higher average token probability.
documents.D13: An automobile insurance policy covers vehicle damage and accident liability. Drivers pay a premium for coverage.
documents.D14: A car park provides parking spaces near the city market. Visitors leave a car while shopping.
documents.D15: Web pages contain links and text. An index stores web content so a search engine can retrieve pages.
